body.statement:
Fix \(\Gamma=4\) and the ATE slice \(3/10\).  There exists \(\eta>0\) such that every one-stratum binary observed law \(P\) satisfying
\[
 \max\{|e_x-1/2|,|p_1-4/5|,|p_0-1/5|\}<\eta
\]
has finite full-law and box-augmented Jensen--CMC frontier values at \(3/10\) and obeys
\[
 C_P(3/10)-\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(3/10)\geq\frac{27}{1820}>0.
\]
Hence the exact rational witness belongs to a nonempty open Euclidean neighborhood of observed laws on which the compatible-full-law cost uniformly and strictly exceeds the value of the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14).
body.proof_tex:
Parameterize a one-stratum binary observed law by
\[
\theta=(e,p_1,p_0)\in(0,1)^3,
\]
where \(e=e_x\).  The four observable probabilities for \((Z,Y)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\) are
\[
ep_1,\qquad e(1-p_1),\qquad(1-e)p_0,\qquad(1-e)(1-p_0).
\tag{22}
\]
On the positive-cell region the inverse map is
\[
e=P(Z=1),\qquad
p_1=\frac{P(Z=1,Y=1)}{P(Z=1)},\qquad
p_0=\frac{P(Z=0,Y=1)}{P(Z=0)},
\tag{23}
\]
so this is a homeomorphic coordinate system for the interior of the observed-law simplex.  Put
\[
\theta_\star=(1/2,4/5,1/5),
\qquad \tau_\star=3/10.
\]
Write \(C_\theta\) and \(\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta\) for the two frontiers at the law indexed by \(\theta\).  The proved theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}strict\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}gap}\) gives
\[
C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)=\frac9{70},qquad
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)=\frac9{91},qquad
g_\star:=\frac9{70}-\frac9{91}=\frac{27}{910}.
\tag{24}
\]

We first prove continuity of the full-law value at \(\theta_\star\).  For a general \(\theta\), define from the frozen scalar program
\[
A_\theta=e(1-p_1),\qquad
B_\theta=(1-e)p_0,\qquad
D_\theta=1-ep_1-(1-e)p_0,
\]
and evaluate \(L_\tau,U_\tau,F_\tau\) at \(\tau=\tau_\star\) and \(\Gamma=4\).  At \(\theta_\star\),
\[
A_{\theta_\star}=B_{\theta_\star}=\frac1{10},qquad
D_{\theta_\star}=\frac12,qquad
\ell=\frac15,qquad u=\frac45.
\]
The three lower-face values are
\[
\frac18,\qquad\frac15,\qquad\frac{13}{50},
\]
and the three upper-face values are
\[
\frac12,\qquad\frac{23}{40},\qquad\frac{11}{25}.
\]
Consequently
\[
[L_{\theta_\star},U_{\theta_\star}]
=[13/50,11/25].
\tag{25}
\]
The point \(v_\star=7/20\) has distance \(9/100\) from both endpoints, and direct substitution gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_{\theta_\star}(v_\star)
&=4\left(\frac1{35}+\frac5{28}+\frac3{40}-\frac14\right)\\
&=4\left(\frac9{280}\right)=\frac9{70}
=C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]

Each candidate face defining \(L_\theta\) and \(U_\theta\) is continuous at \(\theta_\star\), since \(e\in(0,1)\) and therefore \(0<\ell(e)<u(e)<1\).  A finite maximum or minimum of continuous functions is continuous.  Hence, on some neighborhood of \(\theta_\star\), the point \(v_\star\) remains feasible and all feasible intervals lie in a common compact subinterval on which
\[
v,\quad1-\tau_\star-v,\quad e,\quad1-e
\]
are bounded away from zero.  The formula defining \(F_\theta(v)\) is therefore jointly continuous there.

To prove continuity of the value rather than merely pointwise continuity of its objective, take an arbitrary sequence \(\theta_n\to\theta_\star\).  Feasibility of the fixed interior point \(v_\star\), (26), and the scalar-program equality from \(\mathrm{thm{:}binary\mbox{-}phase\mbox{-}catalog}\) give
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}C_{\theta_n}(\tau_\star)
\leq\lim_{n\to\infty}F_{\theta_n}(v_\star)
=C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{27}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), let \(v_n\in[L_{\theta_n},U_{\theta_n}]\) be a minimizer, whose existence is also part of that scalar-program characterization.  Along a subsequence realizing the lower limit, compactness gives a further subsequence, not relabeled, with \(v_n\to v\).  Continuity of the two endpoints implies \(v\in[L_{\theta_\star},U_{\theta_\star}]\), and joint continuity gives
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}C_{\theta_n}(\tau_\star)
=F_{\theta_\star}(v)
\geq C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (27)--(28) prove continuity of \(C_\theta(\tau_\star)\) at \(\theta_\star\).

We next prove continuity of the box-augmented value.  Put \(r_1=ew(\,\cdot\,,1)\) and \(r_0=(1-e)w(\,\cdot\,,0)\).  When \(\Gamma=4\), direct substitution into the odds faces gives their respective lower and upper endpoints
\[
a_1(e)=\frac{1+3e}{4},\quad b_1(e)=4-3e,
\qquad
a_0(e)=\frac{4-3e}{4},\quad b_0(e)=1+3e.
\tag{29}
\]
For \(z\in\{0,1\}\), use \(p_z=p_1\) for \(z=1\) and \(p_z=p_0\) for \(z=0\), and define
\[
\lambda_z(\theta)
=\max\{a_z(e)p_z,\,1-b_z(e)(1-p_z)\},
\qquad
\nu_z(\theta)
=\min\{b_z(e)p_z,\,1-a_z(e)(1-p_z)\}.
\tag{30}
\]
If \(m_z\) is the normalized reweighted mean in arm \(z\), binary support and normalization force
\[
r_z(1)=m_z/p_z,
\qquad r_z(0)=(1-m_z)/(1-p_z).
\tag{31}
\]
Conversely, (31) defines normalized weights for every \(m_z\in(0,1)\).  Applying both box inequalities from (29) to both values in (31) shows, in both directions, that the attainable means are exactly
\[
m_z\in[\lambda_z(\theta),\nu_z(\theta)].
\tag{32}
\]
With \(x=m_0\) and \(m_1=x+\tau_\star\), the relaxed ATE slice is thus exactly
\[
\widetilde L_\theta
:=\max\{\lambda_0(\theta),\lambda_1(\theta)-\tau_\star\}
\leq x\leq
\min\{\nu_0(\theta),\nu_1(\theta)-\tau_\star\}
=:\widetilde U_\theta.
\tag{33}
\]
The algebra in (14), now multiplied by the observed arm probabilities, makes its objective
\[
\widetilde F_\theta(x)
=e\,g_{p_1}(x+\tau_\star)+(1-e)g_{p_0}(x),
\qquad
g_p(m)=\frac{(m-p)^2}{m(1-m)}.
\tag{34}
\]
At \(\theta_\star\), equations (29)--(33) give
\[
[\widetilde L_{\theta_\star},\widetilde U_{\theta_\star}]
=[1/5,1/2].
\tag{35}
\]
The minimizer \(x_\star=7/20\) from \(\mathrm{thm{:}strict\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}gap}\) is at distance \(3/20\) from both endpoints and satisfies
\[
\widetilde F_{\theta_\star}(x_\star)
=\frac9{91}
=\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{36}
\]
All endpoints in (33) are continuous by (29)--(30).  Near (35), the quantities
\[
x,\quad1-x,\quad x+\tau_\star,\quad1-x-\tau_\star
\]
are uniformly positive, so (34) is jointly continuous on a common compact interval.  Repeating the sequence proof in (27)--(28), with the strictly feasible point \(x_\star\) for the upper limit and minimizers in the compact intervals (33) for the lower limit, proves
\[
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(\tau_\star)
\longrightarrow
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)
\quad\text{as }\theta\to\theta_\star.
\tag{37}
\]

By (24), (27)--(28), and (37), there is \(\eta_0>0\) such that the strict cube
\[
B_{\eta_0}:=
\{\theta:\|\theta-\theta_\star\|_\infty<\eta_0\}
\]
keeps both scalar intervals nonempty and satisfies
\[
\left|C_\theta(\tau_\star)-\frac9{70}\right|<\frac{g_\star}{4},
\qquad
\left|\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(\tau_\star)-\frac9{91}\right|<\frac{g_\star}{4}.
\tag{38}
\]
Choose
\[
0<\eta\leq\min\{\eta_0,1/10\}.
\tag{39}
\]
For every \(\theta\in B_\eta\),
\[
 e\geq\frac12-\eta,quad 1-e\geq\frac12-\eta,quad
p_1\geq\frac45-\eta,quad1-p_1\geq\frac15-\eta,quad
p_0\geq\frac15-\eta,quad1-p_0\geq\frac45-\eta.
\tag{40}
\]
It follows from (22) and (40) that every one of the four observable cells has the explicit positive lower bound
\[
P(Z=z,Y=y)
\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)
       \left(\frac15-\eta\right)>0.
\tag{41}
\]
Likewise, both conditional arm variances and the treatment variance obey
\[
p_z(1-p_z)
\geq\left(\frac15-\eta\right)
       \left(\frac45-\eta\right)>0
\quad(z=0,1),
\qquad
e(1-e)\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)^2>0.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the neighborhood is uniformly separated from every observable support boundary relevant to the two programs.

The parameter cube \(B_\eta\) is nonempty and has three-dimensional Lebesgue volume \((2\eta)^3>0\).  Moreover, in the first three observable-cell coordinates in (22), the Jacobian determinant of the parameter-to-law map has absolute value
\[
e(1-e)\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)^2>0.
\tag{43}
\]
The explicit continuous inverse (23) therefore shows directly that its image is a nonempty open Euclidean neighborhood in the interior of the observed-law simplex.  It contains an ordinary Euclidean ball and hence has positive three-dimensional Lebesgue volume; in particular, the neighborhood is not a lower-dimensional path or face.  This records both positive parameter volume and positive observable support.

Finally, subtracting the two inequalities in (38) and using (24) gives, throughout \(B_\eta\),
\[
C_\theta(3/10)-\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(3/10)
\geq g_\star-\frac{g_\star}{2}
=\frac{27}{1820}>0.
\tag{44}
\]
The preserved strict interior points \(v_\star\) and \(x_\star\) prove finiteness of both frontier values there.  Equations (39)--(44) supply the requested uniformly supported, positive-volume open neighborhood and complete the proof.
body.justification: Strictly interior minimizers in both finite-dimensional scalar programs make the exact witness robust: continuity preserves at least half of its rational cost gap on a nonempty open neighborhood.
body.gap: A single numerical or rational witness could be a knife-edge phenomenon; the local theorem rules this out without assuming fixed active odds faces throughout the neighborhood.
body.consumer: The comparison remains informative under small multinomial sampling perturbations of the treated fraction and the two observed arm success probabilities.
